instruction: Highlight all cells in column B that contain values greater than 1.5 by applying a yellow background color to them.

metadata.explanation: Task requires highlighting cells in column B with values > 1.5. Verified with Python: B16(1.6), B17(1.7), B18(1.8), B19(1.9), B20(2.0) are the cells with values > 1.5. Evaluator checks if these 5 cells have background fill applied.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Getter only checks which cells are highlighted, but does NOT verify that highlighted cells contain values > 1.5
False positive vulnerability: Using subset comparison allows extra cells to be highlighted and still pass (e.g., if user highlights B1-B20, test passes as long as B16-B20 are included)
Missing cross-validation: Evaluator doesn't read cell values to confirm only cells with values > 1.5 are highlighted
Color not verified: Instruction specifies 'yellow background color', but getter accepts ANY fill color (red, blue, green would all pass)
No verification that non-highlighted cells have values <= 1.5
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Getter should read both cell values AND highlighting status, returning a dict with cell addresses and their values
Metric should verify: (1) all cells with values > 1.5 are highlighted, (2) all cells with values <= 1.5 are NOT highlighted, (3) use exact set comparison instead of subset
Add color validation to check fill color is yellow (approximate hex ranges for yellow)
Alternative: Create two separate checks - one for correct highlighting of cells > 1.5, another to ensure cells <= 1.5 are not highlighted
